title: Hybrid Private Feature Parity Roadmap — operator UX, upgrade orchestration, pricing bundling (Q3)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: deliver a focused Q3 roadmap that brings parity between Hosted/Dedicated features and Private (VPC/on-prem) operator experience. This ticket defines scope for operator UX (CLI + Console operator view), automated upgrade orchestration with safe rollbacks, and a pricing/bundling model to enable predictable quotes for enterprise customers.

Background: Private customers repeatedly ask for the same operational primitives available in Hosted (e.g., easy canary rollouts, token-level cost telemetry, deterministic upgrade windows) but implemented in a way that fits their networking and compliance constraints. Our Hosted experience is the reference; we aim for parity on the most commonly requested operator flows (deploy, upgrade, rollback, traceability) while leaving full air-gapped edge builds to a later tranche.

Scope (in):
- Operator Console pages: tenant health, per-route latency SLOs, upgrade status, and cost telemetry export.
- Kubernetes operator + optional Ansible wrapper to coordinate rolling upgrades of runtime components with KV-cache warm-start support.
- Runbook templates and CLI shorthand for canary → ramp → full rollout patterns.
- Billing/pricing SKU templates and a quoting calculator for sales to produce consistent reserved/dedicated pricing for private installs.
- Acceptance testing harness that runs against a 3-node private cluster template.

Scope (out):
- Full offline air-gapped installer (targeted for Q4).
- Deep hardware-quantization tuning for every customer GPU variant.

Success metrics:
- 80% reduction in time-to-apply-minor-upgrade for pilot customers (target: from 4 hours → 30 minutes).
- First enterprise pilot uses the new pricing template and receives a quote within 48 hours.
- Operator runbook adoption: 3 pilot customers sign off on runbooks during acceptance.

Notes: this ticket is intentionally cross-functional; product will own acceptance criteria and pricing template, engineering will own the operator and upgrade automation, and DevRel will curate runbooks and examples for SREs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Operator Console shows per-tenant upgrade state and per-route token cost table; 2) Automated rolling upgrade via k8s operator completes a canary followed by safe ramp; system can rollback automatically on health regression; 3) Runbook and CLI allow an operator to perform the standard canary→ramp→full flow in under 30 commands; 4) Pricing template produces a repeatable quote (reserved vs burst) and is validated with Sales on two pilot deals; 5) E2E tests (3-node template) pass nightly for two weeks and pilot customers sign off.

risks:
- Network heterogeneity in customer environments may cause the operator to fail silently; mitigations: increased preflight checks and conservative default timeouts.
- Rolling upgrades may expose stateful KV cache corruption corner-cases; mitigation: KV warm-start + automatic snapshot/restore in the operator.
- Pricing mismatch risk (over/under quoting) — mitigate with two-week pricing runway with Sales pilot and explicit buffer buckets.
- Security concerns about telemetry export from air-gapped customers; workaround: optional telemetry toggles and encrypted export endpoints; full air-gapped flow delayed to Q4.
